correctness.rationale: For n>=3, reduction modulo P=b^(n-2) gives W=L+sP. Carry minimization among lower powers forces at least n-2+bs lower coins, hence s=0. Lower representations then use either n-2 coins (unique), or in base 3 exactly n coins from one split at one of n-3 lower positions. The top pair contributes two optional target collisions precisely when q divides b-1; ternary splits contribute n-3 more precisely when q divides 4. The n=2 case is enumerated exactly. An independent brute-force standard-library verifier passed 1911 complete finite parameter cases, which corroborate but do not prove the unbounded theorem.

value.rationale: The modular single-target collision condition is a natural criterion for exact cyclic coefficient extraction. The family q b^(n-2) fixes the two highest radix positions and leaves all lower digits, a structural rather than arbitrarily selected slice. The theorem provides a complete infinite three-parameter fiber count and a sharply exceptional ternary phase caused by exactly one lower coin split; this is stronger than proving bare validity or recomputing binary minimum values. It does not claim a global least modulus or a wider transform-speed improvement.
